# Pin down the metering data consumption contract for chargeback reporting

## Description

Resolves the strategy's open question about consuming data owned by the in-flight
metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990): what the per-project GPU-hour usage data looks
like, how stable it is, and through what interface the chargeback reporting should
consume it. Produces a documented consumption contract and a decided consumption
approach so that the reporting implementation is not built against a moving schema,
and so that reporting never re-implements metering collection.

## Scope

- Extract the current per-project GPU-hour usage data schema and semantics (fields,
  what counts as a GPU-hour, how usage is attributed to a project) as drafted by the
  metering strategy.
- Assess the schema's stability and finalization outlook, confirmed together with the
  metering strategy owners.
- Decide the consumption approach for reporting: consume the metering schema directly,
  or consume behind a data-access abstraction that isolates reporting from schema
  changes until the metering strategy finalizes.
- Document the consumption contract: the interface reporting will consume, the data
  semantics, and the fallback to apply if the schema shifts before finalization.
- Include a minimal validation fixture that exemplifies the contract shape (a small
  sample demonstrating the interface) — not a usable reporting dataset and not any
  re-implementation of metering collection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the metering strategy's current artifacts, the consumption contract documents
  the per-project GPU-hour usage schema as it stands, together with a stability verdict
  and finalization outlook confirmed with the metering strategy owners.
- The consumption approach (direct consumption vs. data-access abstraction) is decided
  with rationale, and a defined fallback exists for the case where the schema shifts
  before finalization.
- The contract is sufficient for the reporting implementation to proceed: the consuming
  interface and the data semantics (including what counts as a GPU-hour and how usage is
  attributed to a project) are specified.
- A minimal validation fixture demonstrates the contract shape; no metering collection
  is implemented and no usable reporting dataset is produced.

## HLR Traceability

- Gates HLR-1, HLR-2, and the consumption side of HLR-3: the reporting implementation
  consumes the contract this investigation defines.
- Resolves the strategy's Open Question 1 (metering data schema finalizes only when
  RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; report implementation consuming it carries external timing risk).

## Risks

- The metering schema may continue to change until the metering strategy lands. The
  contract must record the agreed fallback path so the reporting implementation can
  proceed under either stability outcome.

# Dashboard admin view for per-project Kueue quota display

## Description

Delivers the administrator-facing view in the Dashboard that lists projects with their
Kueue quota — the part of the chargeback picture that is available without the metering
data. This is the strategy's first shippable user-facing value and can be delivered
while the metering dependency (the in-flight metering strategy RHAISTRAT-9990) matures.

## Scope

- A new administrator-facing section in the Dashboard that lists projects and their
  current Kueue quota, consistent with the platform's Kueue queueing and quota model
  (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue semantics as shipped by the Distributed Workloads stack).
- Determine, within the Kueue quota model, how a project's quota is represented for
  display purposes (a design decision for the implementing team; no new quota concepts
  are invented here).
- Visibility scoped to administrators; regular users do not see the chargeback
  reporting surfaces.
- Quota is read from in-platform Kueue state; no metering data is consumed and no
  metering collection is implemented.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an administrator, the Dashboard provides a view listing projects with their
  current Kueue quota.
- Given a non-administrative user, the administrator chargeback reporting surfaces are
  not visible.
- Quota figures shown for each project are consistent with the platform's Kueue quota
  model (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue semantics as shipped by the Distributed Workloads
  stack): the displayed quota matches the quota derivable from the in-platform Kueue
  state the view reads.
- Given the metering data source is not yet available, the view still presents quota
  information (the capability is usable independently of metering).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1), quota side: the Dashboard admin view showing each project's Kueue quota.
  The current-month consumption side of HLR-3 is delivered by the consumption reporting
  work that builds on this view.

## Assumptions

- Per-project quota is derivable from in-platform Kueue state without code changes in
  the Distributed Workloads stack. If this does not hold, the validation work owned by
  the Distributed Workloads team becomes an implementation epic — confirm at start.
- Confirmation of the quota representation by the Distributed Workloads team (owner of
  the Kueue queueing layer) happens in the downstream validation work; it is not a
  completion condition for this epic.

# Per-project GPU-hour consumption reporting with CSV export and stable API

## Description

Delivers the core chargeback capability: per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over
selectable time ranges computed from the metering data delivered by the in-flight
metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990), the current-month consumption shown against each
project's Kueue quota in the administrator view, and export of those reports as CSV
plus retrieval via a stable API for finance tooling. Reports are denominated in
GPU-hours; currency/cost-rate modelling is out of scope per the strategy.

## Scope

- Compute per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges from
  the per-project GPU-hour usage data delivered by the metering strategy. Collection
  is not re-implemented — reporting only consumes.
- Consume the data through the consumption contract defined by the metering-contract
  investigation. If the metering schema is still volatile, consume behind a
  data-access abstraction and defer direct schema mapping until finalization.
- Add current-month consumption alongside quota in the administrator view, completing
  the consumption-vs-quota comparison.
- Provide CSV export of the reports and retrieval via a stable API suitable for
  finance tooling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the per-project GPU-hour usage data delivered by the metering strategy is
  available, administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over
  selectable time ranges. (HLR-1)
- Reports can be exported as CSV and retrieved via a stable API suitable for finance
  tooling. (HLR-2)
- The administrator view shows current-month consumption against each project's Kueue
  quota. (HLR-3, consumption side)
- Given the metering data source is not yet available, the administrator view retains
  the quota-only presentation — no incomplete or misleading consumption figures are
  shown.
- Report computation consumes metering data only through the agreed consumption
  contract; metering collection is not re-implemented.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges.
- HLR-2 (P1): CSV export and stable API retrieval for finance tooling.
- HLR-3 (P1), consumption side: current-month consumption against each project's Kueue
  quota.

## Risks

- External timing: the metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990) is in flight and its schema
  is not final until it lands. This epic is tier-2 work — it is gated on the
  consumption contract and on metering data availability, while the quota-view and
  contract work proceed independently. Full verification of the consumption
  acceptance criteria requires the metering strategy to have landed and its data to
  be available in the target environment.
- Schema volatility: if the metering schema shifts, the data-access abstraction (or
  the direct mapping, per the decided approach) is rewritten — the fallback is recorded
  in the consumption contract.

# Validate Kueue quota representation in chargeback reporting

## Description

The Distributed Workloads team — owner of the platform's Kueue queueing layer —
validates that the chargeback reporting's quota representation is faithful to Kueue
quota semantics. Distributed Workloads requires no code changes for this strategy;
its involvement is validation of how its quota model is surfaced by the reporting.

## Scope

- Validate that the quota figures displayed in the administrator view — both the
  per-project quota display and the consumption-vs-quota comparison — correctly
  reflect Kueue quota semantics as shipped in the platform (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue
  quota model).
- Validate the project-to-quota attribution used by the reporting (how a project's
  Kueue quota is derived for display).
- Document validation results; discrepancies are reported to the Dashboard
  implementation with severity and a recommended correction (fix-and-retry).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Validation results are documented, covering both the quota display and the
  consumption-vs-quota comparison in the administrator view.
- Quota figures in the reporting match the Kueue quota model as shipped in the
  platform; every discrepancy is reported with a severity and a recommended
  correction.
- The Distributed Workloads team provides an explicit validation verdict (sign-off or
  a findings list) on the quota representation.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): correctness of the Kueue quota side of the administrator view.

## Assumptions

- Distributed Workloads is a passive component in this strategy: quota is consumed via
  the in-platform Kueue queueing layer with no code changes on that side. If surfacing
  per-project quota turns out to require Distributed Workloads changes, this epic
  becomes an implementation epic — confirm at start.
